A POST form needs no token field: the runtime adds `_csrf` to every form with method="post" or an hx-post/put/patch/delete attribute (HTMX requests also send the X-CSRF-Token header). Don't write one: `{{csrf}}` renders empty in mustache and `{{.csrf}}` in gotmpl.

A search or filter form is a GET form: `<form method="get" action="/events"><input name="city"><button>Filter</button></form>`. Its fields become the next page's `{{param_city}}` / `.param_city` / `:param_city`. A form the browser submits with GET (method="get", hx-get, or no method) never gets the CSRF token, so it never lands in the URL. The write gate accepts method="get" and hx-get forms; a form with inputs and no method at all is refused (next entry).
The write gate refuses a form with inputs and no method, HTMX attribute or directive (dead-form), a password form without method="post", nested forms and `_method` overrides.
